readiness.evidencePolicy: Generated documents and asserted decisions are design evidence only. Schema validation, mock tests, account plans and deployed-system tests require separate receipts tied to the exact configuration. This export does not ingest implementation evidence.

requirements.statement: The system shall accept PDF invoices and persist supplier, invoice date, total and currency in a review queue, linked to the original document; failed or uncertain extraction shall remain visible for staff resolution.
requirements.rationale: Makes the requested outcome observable and prevents incomplete or uncertain extraction from bypassing review.
requirements.basis: “Users upload PDF invoices. Extract the supplier, invoice date, total and currency into a review queue.” Source evidence and handling of uncertain extraction are engineering proposals.

requirements.statement: Accounting submission shall require an authorized reviewer’s recorded approval of the exact result revision and destination operation; changing the result shall require renewed approval, and extraction alone shall never authorize submission.
requirements.rationale: Prevents model output or unauthorized users from triggering accounting actions, and prevents approval from being reused after the reviewed result changes.
requirements.basis: “A reviewer approves a result before it is sent to our existing accounting API.” Server-side reviewer authorization and revision-bound approval are proposed controls.

requirements.statement: Repeated delivery and worker retries shall not create duplicate invoice records or accounting submissions. Persist workflow state and operation identity durably, retry only under a tested destination idempotency contract, and hold ambiguous outcomes for reconciliation before resubmission.
requirements.rationale: Retries after a crash or lost response can create duplicate financial records; durable identities and destination acceptance are necessary to establish safe delivery.
requirements.basis: “Delivery can repeat; retries must not create duplicate invoices.” Durable operation identity, uncertain-outcome fencing and reconciliation are proposed engineering mechanisms supported by the supplied durable-approval practice.

requirements.statement: Documents and extracted data shall be stored and processed in Australia. Apply this boundary to inference, recovery copies, diagnostics containing those data and accounting delivery. Flag unverified service/model availability and processing geography; do not enable an overseas fallback.
requirements.rationale: Personal data could leave Australia through inference, backups, diagnostics or accounting delivery even when primary storage is Australian. This proposed requirement makes those paths subject to acceptance.
requirements.basis: “they may contain personal data” and “Keep documents and extracted data in Australia; flag unverified service availability.”

requirements.statement: The system shall retain invoice originals and extraction audit history for 90 days and implement scheduled retention cleanup. Document and test the retention clock, object-version handling and backup expiry before claiming a final deletion deadline.
requirements.rationale: Retention must cover original objects and durable audit records consistently; backup and object-version expiry need acceptance to avoid retaining hidden copies indefinitely.
requirements.basis: “Keep originals and extraction audit history for 90 days.”

measure.metric: Original and extraction audit retention period

requirements.statement: Design and qualify asynchronous intake for approximately 500 invoices per day, using durable queueing and recoverable processing. Establish tested burst capacity and processing completion times without treating the daily average as a peak-rate guarantee.
requirements.rationale: The stated daily volume informs queue capacity and worker sizing; durable intake must preserve invoices during processing delays. No peak rate or completion deadline was supplied.
requirements.basis: “around 500 per day” and the existing asynchronous invoice review workflow.

requirements.statement: Persist job state and queue/outbox changes transactionally, preserve invoice/job identity across retries, and recover stalled workers with lease fencing. Bound retry attempts and deadlines; retain exhausted jobs in a durable dead-letter/recovery state with reason and audit history. Authorized recovery shall preserve identity and approval constraints. Demonstrate crash recovery, retry exhaustion and recovery without duplicate invoices or submissions.
requirements.rationale: Durable failure records and controlled recovery prevent exhausted or interrupted jobs from disappearing or creating duplicate work. Lease fencing and recovery procedures are proposed engineering controls.
requirements.basis: “Use a durable job queue, stable invoice/job identity, bounded retries, a dead-letter/recovery path, approval checks and an idempotent outbound operation.”

requirements.statement: Run extraction asynchronously after durable intake and return a stable job reference. Persist and expose processing, review and failure/recovery status to authorized staff independently of the upload request or browser session. Do not impose an unconfirmed completion-time target.
requirements.rationale: Several-minute jobs must survive browser disconnection and HTTP timeouts. Persisted status lets staff distinguish queued, processing, review and recovery states.

requirements.statement: Integrate with the existing externally managed accounting API without provisioning or modifying that system. Accept administrator-supplied endpoint and credentials through protected destination configuration. Qualify authorization, Australian processing geography, normalized-action-v1 compatibility, durable idempotency and receipt reconciliation before enabling delivery.
requirements.rationale: Preserving the existing accounting system avoids accidental provisioning or ownership changes; a protected configuration boundary prevents secrets entering project records.
requirements.basis: “The accounting system already exists. An administrator will supply its endpoint and credentials; treat it as external, not a new system to provision.”
